proposals.before: Chen Tanlang, Prince Min of Nankang, was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's maternal uncle.
proposals.after: Chen Tanlang, Prince Min of Nankang, was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's younger brother by the same mother.
proposals.reason: Chinese 高祖母弟 means Gaozu's uterine younger brother (母弟), not maternal uncle; Gaozu later calls Xiuxian 此弟.

proposals.before: Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, younger brother of the Founder's mother.
proposals.after: Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's younger brother by the same mother.
proposals.reason: 母弟 is uterine younger brother of Gaozu, not younger brother of Gaozu's mother.

proposals.before: In Tiankang year two, when peace was made with Qi, the court first learned he was dead.
proposals.after: In Tianjia year two, when peace was made with Qi, the court first learned he was dead.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang (天康 is a different later era).

proposals.before: In the second year of Tiankang, when Qi made peace, they first learned of it.
proposals.after: In the second year of Tianjia, when Qi made peace, they first learned of it.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 romanization should be Tianjia.

proposals.before: In Tiankang year one an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang is held in Qi and cannot return; the ancestral temple is being restored and needs a master—let his eldest son Fangtai be heir of Nankang and succeed the title."
proposals.after: In Tianjia year one an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang is held in Qi and cannot return; the ancestral temple is being restored and needs a master—let his eldest son Fangtai be heir of Nankang and succeed the title."
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang.

proposals.before: In the first year of Tiankang, an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, cut off in the Qi court, his return uncertain; the state temple is being restored and sacrifices need a master—his eldest son Fangtai may be made Heir of Nankang and succeed the Prince of Nankang."
proposals.after: In the first year of Tianjia, an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, cut off in the Qi court, his return uncertain; the state temple is being restored and sacrifices need a master—his eldest son Fangtai may be made Heir of Nankang and succeed the Prince of Nankang."
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang.

proposals.before: During Tiankang he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linru.
proposals.after: During Tianjia he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linru.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang.

proposals.before: In the Tiankang era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru county.
proposals.after: In the Tianjia era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru county.
proposals.reason: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang.

proposals.before: When Gui and the rest were put to death, the northerners also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; he was twenty-eight. (The text supplies the missing word "year".)
proposals.after: When Gui and the rest were put to death, the northerners also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; he was twenty-eight.
proposals.reason: Parenthetical editorial note is not part of the translation of the Chinese.

decisions.reason: 高祖母弟 means Gaozu’s uterine younger brother (母弟), not maternal uncle; the proposed phrasing restores that kinship.
高祖母弟 parses as Gaozu’s 母弟 (uterine younger brother), not ‘younger brother of the Founder’s mother’; the replacement matches that reading.
天嘉 romanizes as Tianjia; Tiankang would be 天康, a different Chen era name.
天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang; only the era romanization needs correction.
天嘉元年 is the first year of Tianjia; Tiankang misreads 嘉 as 康.
Literal field has the same 天嘉→Tianjia error; the proposed romanization is correct.
天嘉中 is during the Tianjia era, not Tiankang.
Same 天嘉→Tianjia correction as the idiomatic field; the rest of the literal already matches the Chinese.
時年二十八 supports ‘he was twenty-eight’; the parenthetical about supplying ‘year’ is translator commentary, not Chinese text.
